plan.title: Entropy: Why Everything Spreads Out
plan.description: Entropy measures how evenly energy is spread out in a system. The second law of thermodynamics says that in an isolated system it never decreases, which is why some processes can't be undone.

beats.narration: Why does a hot coffee always cool down, but never heats itself back up? The answer is one word: entropy.
Entropy measures how spread out energy is. Concentrated energy means low entropy. Evenly dispersed energy means high entropy.
The second law says an isolated system's entropy cannot decrease. Energy spreads out, and that makes some processes irreversible.

props.text: Entropy never decreases in an isolated system.

beats.narration: So time's arrow is just energy spreading out. Remember: nature drifts toward even.
